Lambert abandoned the black coat and delivered Sam Cooke’s “A Change Is Gonna Come” while dressed in a shiny silver suit. Allen’s response from the judges was not as positive after he performed Marvin Gaye’s “What’s Goin’ On.”

“I thought it was too laid back for a night like this,” Cowell said, awarding the second round to Lambert.

Allen, by contrast, had trouble keeping his pitch steady throughout the performance, though the judges were gentler in their criticism this time.

“You have thoroughly, thoroughly deserved to be standing on that stage tonight, congratulations,” Cowell told him.

“There was a lot of lyric, and it was a big song,” Lambert said. “But it’s a beautiful song.”

“He’s always giving me stuff to change about mine ... to make it better,” Allen told reporters.

## Adam Lambert: dramatic, polished, and built for the stage

Adam Lambert came into the finale as the season’s most explosive performer, and his song choices leaned into that reputation.

### “Mad World”
Adam’s reprise of **“Mad World”** was one of the night’s most anticipated moments because it had already become a signature performance for him earlier in the season. He brought back the haunting, theatrical mood that made the song stand out the first time: controlled vocals, dramatic phrasing, and a dark, cinematic atmosphere.

### Judge feedback for Adam
The judges generally praised Adam’s command of the stage and his vocal control. **Simon Cowell** and the panel often framed him as the more technically dazzling contestant, someone who could take a song and turn it into an event. Even when the comments weren’t unanimous on every choice, the tone was clear: Adam was a major vocalist with star quality.

## Kris Allen: intimate, musical, and emotionally direct

Kris Allen’s strength throughout the season was his ability to make songs feel personal. He wasn’t as flashy as Adam, but he had a quiet confidence and a knack for reshaping familiar material into something intimate and believable.

### “Ain’t No Sunshine”
Kris’s reprise of **“Ain’t No Sunshine”** was arguably his strongest moment of the finale. Seated at the piano, he delivered a restrained but soulful performance that highlighted his phrasing, musicality, and emotional connection to the lyric.

Where Adam’s performances often felt theatrical and expansive, Kris’s best work felt close-up and conversational. “Ain’t No Sunshine” played directly into that advantage. It reminded viewers that Kris had built his fan base not through spectacle, but through taste, sincerity, and smart musical choices.

### Judge feedback for Kris
The judges were impressed by Kris’s authenticity and musicianship, especially on “Ain’t No Sunshine.” They praised the way he could interpret a song without oversinging it. ## “No Boundaries”: the coronation song problem

Both finalists also had to perform **“No Boundaries,”** the official winner’s single co-written by Kara DioGuardi. As with many “American Idol” coronation songs, it was designed to be inspirational, soaring, and broadly uplifting—but it didn’t fit either contestant perfectly.

For Kris, “No Boundaries” sat awkwardly in places. The song’s big key changes and inspirational-pop structure didn’t naturally match his laid-back, acoustic-leaning style. He worked through it with sincerity, but it wasn’t the kind of song that showed him at his best.

### Adam Lambert’s “No Boundaries”

The judges’ reactions to “No Boundaries” were more mixed than their responses to the contestants’ stronger individual choices. The criticism was less about the singers’ abilities and more about the song itself. It was a typical finale single: earnest, high-reaching, and a little generic. Both Kris and Adam did what they could with it, but neither version became the defining performance of the night.

The finale worked because Kris and Adam were so different.
